HOW WRONG WOULD THIS HAVE TO BE TO FAIL. At the worst corner the demand would have

becomes 9.21%. None of those reverses it.

P4 THE REPLACEMENT FRACTION
molecule-weighted f = 25.7%  -- the proteasome's currency, 4,821 proteins
mass-weighted     f = 27.1%  -- the ribosome's currency, 4,179 proteins
so 27% of every residue laid down replaces protein that has been destroyed;
only 73% adds new mass.
(a) gate: the two currencies agree to within 10% -- gap 1.4%  PASS
a gap would mean protein SIZE is coupled to turnover. The gap here is 1.4%, i.e.
5% of the fraction itself, and it points the mass currency higher, so short-lived proteins are marginally LARGER.
A proteasome's bill and a ribosome's bill are therefore the same bill to within
a couple of points, and neither machine's view of turnover misleads about the
other's.
(b) gate: mass-weighted within 2x of loop 74's corrected 36.9% (recorded 29.2%)
ratio 0.734x, band 18.4%-73.8%  PASS

interpretation: A destroys the abundance-turnover pairing entirely, B keeps it at

A fires and B does not, so the information in the load lives at DECILE
resolution: knowing which abundance decile a protein sits in fixes the load to
within the null spread, and its individual half-life adds nothing on top of
that. That is a statement about how much per-protein data a turnover model
actually needs, and it was not knowable without running both nulls.

P6 THE FAME CONTROL, AND WHAT THIS DOES NOT GIVE
pubs vs per-protein proteolytic load +0.2800   (n 4,821)
copies vs per-protein load           +0.8895
pubs vs copies                       +0.2568
pubs vs protein half-life            +0.0362
half-life vs per-protein load        -0.0015
copies vs protein half-life          +0.4182  <- the direct form of what
null A detected. A positive value here IS 'abundant proteins are long-lived'. If
it is near zero while null A fires, the null is being carried by the extreme tail
rather than by a monotone trend, which is what P5's tail check tests.
gate: |rho(pubs, load)| < |rho(copies, load)| -- fame must explain the load LESS well
than the abundance the load is built from
P6 PASS -- the per-protein decomposition is carried by abundance, not by attention
the proteasome subunits' own fame: median pubs 232 against 87 for the covered proteome (2.67x)
-- the particle count rests on a well-studied family, so its copy numbers are as
likely as any to be right, and equally likely to be over-detected. Reported.
WHAT THIS DOES NOT GIVE. Not all degradation is proteasomal: autophagy and lysosomal
proteolysis handle bulk protein and organelles, so assigning every destroyed molecule
to the 26S proteasome makes P3 CONSERVATIVE -- the real proteasomal load is below the
demand computed here, and a pass bounds the answer rather than measuring occupancy.
Nothing here supplies ubiquitination kinetics, substrate queueing, or the difference
between a 40-residue substrate and a 4,000-residue one, which 1-3 s averages over.
The 20S/19S stoichiometry (P1) remains a factor-of-two exposure in the direction that
helps the gate, which is why P3 is evaluated at the worst corner and not the middle.
